newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds up, U.S. rate woes seen returning.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds up, U.S. rate woes seen returning.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late Tuesday as the market rose on short-covering but the gains were not seen sustained in coming sessions as worries over U.S. interest rates were expected to re-emerge.
"Everybody has been playing the market short," said a trader at a local bank. That meant a rise early Tuesday attracted some buyer interest from local banks.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 1/4 at 89-5/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.41 to 128.01.
But, "there is no genuine money coming into the market," said another trader, predicting that the "traders play" will continue to dominate.

That means the market is set to resume its U.S. indicator watch, following Treasuries' changing perceptions on U.S. inflation and rates. Friday's release of U.S. inflation figures will be this week's highlight, said traders.
On the domestic scene Tuesday, the Economy Ministry reported an Argentine trade deficit of $134 million in February, compared with $102 million a year earlier.
Call money rates fell to 5.88 percent from 5.98 percent.
